שמו עליו משמר. פ"א יצא לחוץ וחפר קברו של אייבשיצער, כמעט קט הגיע לארונו, לולי שראוהו ומצאוהו עוסק בחפירות הקבר, ומנעוהו בכח והחזירוהו לבית האסורים וכבלוהו, אחר נטלו הכבלים ממנו ועזבוהו לנפשו, כי חשבוהו שנתיישבה דעתו, שהיה אומר תמיד דברי קדושה, ואמר כ"פ שרוצה לטבול עצמו, ויהי כי ראה עצמו בלי שמירה, יצא ורץ עד מקום המים וטבל בהם, אבל שקע בהם ורצה להציל עצמו לאחוז באיזה דבר, כאשר העיד נכרי שראהו מרחוק, אבל לא יכול כי היה חלש ונטבע מיד, והביאוהו לקבר ישראל בכבוד. לויה גדולה עשו לו סמוך לכניסת שבת קדש. שנת תקכ"ט.
בשבט התועדו ג"ק על אודות מינוי רב חדש, והיו רבים חפצים להשיבני לנחלת אבותי, וכשעמדו למנין לעשות רשימה מהראוים לאצטלא זו, נעשית מריבה ביניהם על אודותי, וכמעט היה הרוב על צדי, וכך היה בודאי אם היו עושים דבר זה בגלוי, לא היה אדם אחר עולה להתמנות רב בג"ק בפעם הזאת; אכן התחכמו שלשה מאויבי, הלא הם ריש בריוני יחילכי וואלף, יעקב שלעזינגר, הירץ שטאר, ובטלו הוועד ההוא; אח"כ התחבלו להפיק מזמתם לדבר על לב הנועדים לשוב להתועד מחדש על עסק זה, ולקבץ דעות בהסתר והעלם מכל וכל, דהיינו ע"י שיעשו מיני עגולים שונים, באופן שהאחד יורה על הן והשני על לאו, ועשו שתי קופות מהעיגולים, כדי שיקח כל אחד מהנבררים לחות דעתו, באופן שיקח אחד מהעיגולים שירצה בהסתר, בלי שיראה אדם מאיזה הוא לוקח ומניחם בקלפי, אח"כ ימנו העיגולים ויראו מאיזה הרוב, ונתרצו יחד בזה, ובתוך כך הלכו המתנגדים הנ"ל, ופתו והסיתו קצתם עד שסרו למשמעתם אחד או שנים; אולי ברצי כסף נתרצו להם לחזור בהם ולבגוד בי, ולא דאגו מעתה כי עכ"פ לא יודע מי הוא אשר חזר בו מדעתו הקודמת ומאן בי, ועשו כן והצליח בידם מה שרצו לסלקני מן מנין הראוים. מעתה חשבו שכבר עלה בידיהם ג"כ, לבחור ביוסף מוקיר שבתא שטיינ' אב"ד מפירדא, וחשבוהו כאלו הוא כבר אחר מעשה, אבל [טעו] כי אחר זה כשעשו בוררים לקבל הרב החדש, ואע"פ שהיה נדמה לכל שהרוב היה לצדם, אכן מה' היתה שקצתם בקשו לעמוד על דעתי להיכן נוטה, וע"כ הוצרכתי לתת דעתי והסכמתי להרב מבראד מכמה טעמים, עד שעלתה בידנו ונבחר זה האיש לרב דג"ק על ידי בס"ד.

set a guard over him. Once he went out and dug up the grave of Eybeschütz ⟨S: "the abominable"⟩, and had almost reached his coffin, had they not seen
him and found him busy digging the grave; they stopped him by force, brought him back to the prison and put him in chains. Afterwards they took the
chains off him and left him to himself, for they thought his mind had settled, since he was always saying holy words. Several times he said that he
wanted to immerse himself; and when he saw himself without a guard, he went out and ran to a place of water and immersed himself in it. But he sank in
it, and wanted to save himself by catching hold of something ⟨S: a short word beside the line, perhaps "אל"(?)⟩, as a gentile who saw him from afar testified; but he could not, for he was weak, and he
drowned at once. They brought him to a Jewish grave with honour; they gave him a great funeral close to the coming in of the holy Sabbath. The year
[5]529 ⟨S: "the year [5]525"⟩.

In Shevat the Three Communities assembled about the appointment of a new rabbi, and many wanted to bring me back to the inheritance of my fathers.
When they stood to vote, to draw up a list of those worthy of this mantle, a quarrel arose among them about me, and the majority was almost on my
side; and so it would surely have been, had they done this thing openly: no other man would have been appointed rabbi of the Three Communities this
time. But three of my enemies ⟨S: "sinners of Israel"(?)⟩ acted cunningly — namely the chief ruffian Yeḥielke Wolf, Jacob Schlesinger and Hertz Stör —
and they broke up that meeting. Afterwards they schemed to carry out their plot: to persuade those assembled to meet again afresh on this matter, and to
collect the opinions in secret, hidden altogether; that is, by making different kinds of balls, so that one would indicate yes and the other no. They
made two boxes of the balls, so that each of the electors would take one, to express his opinion, taking whichever ball he wished in secret, without
anyone seeing from which he took it, and put them in the ballot box; afterwards they would count the balls and see which had the majority. They all
agreed to this. Meanwhile the said opponents went and enticed and incited some of them, until one or two came over to their side — perhaps with
"pieces of silver" (Ps. 68:31) they were won over to go back and betray me — and they no longer worried, since in any case it would not be known who it
was that had gone back on his former opinion and refused me. So they did, and they succeeded in what they wanted, to remove me from the number of the
worthy. Now they thought they had already succeeded also in choosing Joseph "who honours the Sabbath" Steinhardt, head of the court of Fürth, and they
regarded him as if it were already done. But [they erred]: for afterwards, when they appointed electors to receive the new rabbi, although it seemed to
all that the majority was on their side, yet it was from the Lord that some of them sought to learn which way my opinion inclined; and so I had to give
my opinion and agreement for the rabbi of Brody, for several reasons, until we succeeded and this man was chosen rabbi of the Three Communities through
me, with the help of Heaven.

the Hamburg [synagogue] in London [a] — also through my effort and work, with God's help, for some time; and it had already been given up, for he had

opposing side to cancel his appointment were of no avail. Even after he had already been accepted properly and in due form, some individuals of the
said side conspired against him and wrote him a letter of rebellion and refusal, with a warning not to come to them, for they would refuse him. This was
done through the go-between, "the disgrace of the generation", a pupil of A. A. ⟨S: "the abominable, m[ay the name of the wicked] r[ot]"⟩, who is there; he
exerted himself in this and also sent such a gathered and tangled letter by the post, thinking to frighten and alarm me, so that I would keep my son
from going there. But the other side, who wanted him, encouraged and urged me on this, not to heed the deceitful doings of the opponents; and so I did,
and warned my son not to turn to the words of the ugly letter. And he did and prospered, thank God: he came here, and spent this festival of Weeks with
them, and all the notables of the Three Communities did him honour, and he found favour in the eyes of all who saw him. He travelled from here and
reached the place of his desire and the seat of his honour in the middle of Tammuz, and was received with great honour, and they rejoiced in him "as
with the joy in harvest" (Isa. 9:2). "The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light" (Isa. 9:1), and they praised him greatly. Letters
reached me from there that even the enemies had turned into friends, and they are glad and rejoice in him "as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride"
(Isa. 62:5). May it be the will of the Master of mercy that he prosper and rise higher and higher, to bring merit to himself and to others with him,
and that He grant him sons, and gladden me with my descendants, may they live, in general and in particular. May it be His will. Amen!

At that same time I set up in the town of Gens(?) [b] the scholar R. Joshua Lipschitz, who had been persecuted on account of my ruling which I had
asked him about words of Torah; and with God's help I brought him to a place of rest with honour.

לדבר מאומה רע כנ"ל; לכן לא יכולתי לפעול עמו דבר, ונשארתי לבדי, אין מתעורר [לעמוד עמדי] ולא מחזיק בידי; אכן אלהי אבי היה עמדי, לא אירא מרגשת פועלי און וחורשי רע בלבבם, בצל ידו החביאני ובכנפי חמלתו הסתירני. אמנם הכרוז הנ"ל בבהכ"נ שלי עשה רושם. מיד תוך ד"י ימים נכוה בגחלת הכרוז [א] ישראל שווערין, מחזיק בכלב פרוסטיץ הנ"ל להיות שם מורה צעקה, והתריתי כל הקיץ שעבר, כתבתי לשווערין שיסירו האיסור מן [העדה] פן יהא להם למוקש והיא לא תצלח, ולא אבו שמוע אלי [ב]. ויהי ביום ה"ר [ג] נכווה ברותחין ששפכה עליו משרתת הבית ונבושה עורו, והיה בסכנה גדולה וביסורים מכוערים כמה שבועות, ולבסוף נסדר לו מרופא להקיז דם והעלתה המכה צמחים; וגם בזאת הלך ולא שם לבו לדבר ה', ועודנו מחזיק ברעתו לעזור לרשע ולסייע עוברי עבירה, להיות לו סורר ומורה הפושע פרוסטיצר.
בחורף הלז שילהי כסלו נמניתי אני לבורר של אשה קילא לגמור דינה ותביעתה מיורשי בעלה, וישבתי פעמים עם הרב אב"ד והדיין רל"פ, והדברים ארוכים כתובים אצלי בקונטרס בפ"ע. בו בפרק חזר והתעולל בי מיחוש גיד הזהוב, כי נתקררתי אחר חמום גדול שהי"ל בישיבת הדיינין הנ"ל, ובהיותי מושך דם כמעין ביושבי בהכ"נ, ובצאתי נפלתי לארץ מרוב חולשה, והיתה בהלה גדולה בביתי ובקהלה, וה' חמל עלי ושב רוחי אלי; אך כמה שבועות לא שקטה רתיחת המעים, והיה הדם כנחל שוטף גם הוחלשו כחותי מאד, לא הייתי בקו הבריאות כמו שני חדשים; אחר חזרתי לאיתני הראשון ת"ל חיי. בו בטוח לבי ונעזרתי, הוא ית' יחייני לעבודתו ויראתו!
בר"ח אדר הגיעני מכתב על הפאשט מרעכניץ, מקום אשר ליב שטאטשטיץ אסו"ר שם למורה איסור והיתר, מודיעים אותי הכשרים שבקהל שם, ששמעו ידעו וראו העתק הכרוז שנעשה בבהכ"נ שלי, על האנשים הנ"ל, ופחדו ורהו והיו רוצים לגרש הרב שלהם הנ"ל בגלל הכרוז [ד], אך קמו בני בליעל המחזיקים בידו וההבילו הכרוז,
[א] עיין בס' התאבקות בחלק גת דרוכה (דף ע"ג) ושם נאמר כך: תוך ד"י אחר וכו' ונכוה בו.

to say anything bad, as above. So I could not achieve anything with him, and I remained alone, with no one stirring [to stand with me] and no one
supporting me. Yet "the God of my father has been with me" (Gen. 31:5); I will not fear the throng of the workers of iniquity and those who devise
evil in their heart. "In the shadow of His hand He hid me" (Isa. 49:2), and in the wings of His compassion He concealed me.

Indeed the said proclamation in my synagogue made an impression. At once, within fourteen days, Israel Schwerin was burnt by the coal of the
proclamation ⟨S: "the ban"(?)⟩ [a] — he who supported the said dog Prossnitz to be teacher there, "a teacher of outcry". I had warned all the past
summer, writing to Schwerin that they should remove the forbidden thing from [the congregation], lest it be a snare to them, and that it would not
prosper; but they would not listen to me [b]. And on the day of H. R. ⟨S: a word, partly read: "H…"(?)⟩ [c] he was scalded with boiling water
that the housemaid poured over him, and his skin was scorched; he was in great danger and in ugly sufferings for several weeks, and in the end a
physician arranged for him to be bled, and the wound came up in sores. Yet with this too he went on and did not set his heart to the word of the Lord;
he still holds fast to his wickedness ⟨S: "to his insolence"(?)⟩, to help the wicked and support transgressors, so that the transgressor Prossnitz ⟨S:
"m[ay the name of the wicked] r[ot]"⟩ may be for him a stubborn and rebellious [son].

In this winter, at the end of Kislev, I was appointed arbiter for the woman Kila, to settle her case and her claim against her husband's heirs. I sat
several times with the rabbi, head of the court, and the judge R. L. P.; the matter is long and is written down by me in a separate quire. At that time
the ailment of the golden vein again attacked me, for I caught a chill after a great heat that I had at the said sitting of the judges; and as I was
drawing blood like a spring while sitting in the synagogue ⟨S: a word, partly read⟩, when I went out I fell to the ground from great weakness. There was
great alarm in my house and in the community; and the Lord had pity on me and my spirit returned to me. But for several weeks the boiling of the bowels
did not subside, and the blood was like a rushing stream; my strength was also greatly weakened, and I was not within the line of health for about two
months. Afterwards I returned to my former strength, thank God who lives. In Him my heart trusts and I am helped; may He, blessed be He, keep me alive
for His service and His fear!

On the New Moon of Adar a letter reached me by the post from Rechnitz, where Leib Stadtschitz(?), a dog [and] ... (אסו"ר), is teacher of the forbidden
and permitted. The upright of the community there informed me that they had heard, known and seen a copy of the proclamation ⟨S: "the ban"(?)⟩ made in
my synagogue against the said men ⟨S: a three-line note, partly read: "the unclean … the band of Belial … who were …"⟩; and they were afraid and

Some time later the gaon Ya'avetz learned of this matter in detail, and he wrote to Rechnitz on the 3rd of Adar of the year 5526 [1766] as follows:
"The letter that you wrote to the community here surely came into the hand of one of his admirers, and he hid it and showed it to no one else; no
upright man's eye fell upon it. We asked and inquired well, and no one knows anything of whether such a letter reached the people of the community
here. Therefore without doubt that reckless and empty fellow who received the letter answered you in the name of this whole community, by forgery and
deceit, as if it had been done with their knowledge — and perhaps he even signed all their names under it; and all is vanity and a complete lie,
invented out of his own heart. Therefore know for certain that the letter you received from Hamburg is "a driven lie" [b]." The words of Ya'avetz
made an impression on the community, and they removed their rabbi, whom for some years they had pursued in the holy community of P. B. and in Prague,
without prevailing against him [c]. In this year, on the 14th of Iyyar, the gaon Ya'avetz wrote a letter to his relative and pupil, our teacher R.
Jacob Katz, about the matter of the sect of Sh. Tz., which had then arisen anew in Teplitz [d]. And in the year 5527, on the 26th of Tishri [1766],
the gaon Ya'avetz received a letter from the sage R. M. D. of the city of Berlin, as follows: "Blessed be the Lord, who has not left us without a
redeemer, and has raised up for us our master, teacher and rabbi, to keep his charge, and he has risked his life to avenge the vengeance of His Torah.
Who is like him in an orphaned generation, fencing the fence and standing in the breach? Who will rise up for us against evil-doers who speak
rebellion against the Lord and defy the armies of the God of Israel,

who will stand up for us against the workers of iniquity (cf. Ps. 94:16), who lead the heart of the men of Israel astray to deny the homilies and
traditions of our sages of blessed memory, by whose mouth we live — had not the Lord stirred up the spirit of my teacher, whose heart is like the heart
of a lion? He laughs at the voice of the fools and is not dismayed by their multitude; "He is in one [mind], and who can turn Him?" (Job 23:13) — and
who can turn back his strong hand, the uplifted hand of the Mighty One of Jacob, to break the teeth of the wicked and to pull down the great teeth of
the young lions (cf. Ps. 58:7), whether with straight and clear arguments, built on the foundations of the Torah and reason, or by pursuing them in the
sea of the Kabbalah, in secrets and allusions, gematrias, notarikon and initials, until no place is left for them to flee there and hide with their
enchantments; and if they go down "to the bars of the pit" (Job 17:16), "there too his hand will lead them and his right hand will hold them" (cf. Ps.
139:10) [a].

In the year 5528 [1768] the gaon Ya'avetz received a letter from Petersburg saying that the sect of Sh. Tz., seeing that their hope among the
Christians in Poland had failed, had gone to the land of Muscovy with letters of recommendation and petitions in their hands, to bring their head,
Jacob Frank, out of prison [b]. At that time Ya'avetz saw fit to bring out in print the book Mitpaḥat Sefarim, whose subject is to show the
strange things found in the holy Zohar, the Ra'aya Meheimna and the Tikkunim, which had been hidden in his heart for many years, because the hour
required it [c]. In this year 5528 [1768] he also brought out in print his book Tzitzim u-Feraḥim, which is the secrets of the letters, allusions
and gematrias in the way of the Kabbalah and the hidden lore, to show that "his hands are sufficient for him" (Deut. 33:7) in this too; and then the
printing of his book Mor u-Ketzi'ah, parts 1 and 2, was also finished. In the year 5529 [1769] he printed the book Ha-Pedut ve-ha-Purkan of our
master Saadiah Gaon, and at its end he added "A Terrible Deed in Podolia", seven pages about the sect of Sh. Tz. [d]. In the year 5532 [1772] there
was an exchange of letters between him and the sage R. M. D. on the matter of delaying the burial of the dead [e]. In the year 5534 [1773], on the
9th of Marḥeshvan, the sage R. M. D. asked him a question about the saying of Maimonides, of blessed memory: "Whoever accepts the seven commandments and
is careful to do them is one of the pious of the nations of the world", etc.; and he, Ya'avetz, answered him according to the good hand of the Lord upon
him [f].

In those days a strong longing awoke in the heart of the gaon Ya'avetz to go to the Land of Israel and settle in the land of his fathers, in the city
of the graves of his grandfather, of blessed memory [g]; and he then spoke about

the heart of the parnassim and leaders of Altona to buy his house, to be a landed possession for them, for their great synagogue was too small to hold

the days of his life he did not depart from the tent of Torah. Four days before his death he sent to the grammarian, the gaon R. Solomon Dubno, the

which the gaon Ya'avetz died, near the Sabbath, his dust returned to the earth and his spirit to God (cf. Eccl. 12:7), and all the people of the town
mourned him with a very heavy mourning. And this is the tombstone set up on his grave [b], and on it are written these words:

Tombstone

The master of the Jews, the best of the sages.
Howl and lament! Is it not heard in the camp of the Hebrews that a burning fire has burnt in it?
Ornament and glory were cast from her head at the death of a wise man, mighty, "turning back the battle at the gate" (Isa. 28:6).
Holy and pure from the womb, from the dawn [of his days]; he made nights like days in the Torah of the Lord, "ordered and sure" (2 Sam. 23:5).
By his holy works, "their polishing of sapphire" (Lam. 4:7), he spread to the corners [of the earth] his light, in the hidden and in the revealed, clear
law.
The fear of the Lord, the reproof of instruction, and all the hidden things of wisdom, he brought out by them to the light.
A great prince has fallen in Israel. Do you not know that the Lord has taken the master from over our head (cf. 2 Kgs. 2:3), and the covering of
precious stone has been removed (cf. Ezek. 28:13)?
Many are his Torah and his wisdom, written and still hidden in his house of study; may light shine upon him.

ל ו יאות למבכי ולמעבד הספדא על כי חומה היה לנו ביום זעם ועברה צרה כמבכירה.
ה"ה הגאון הגדול המפורסם בקי בכל חדרי תורה בנגלה ובנסתר ובכל החכמות כל רז לא אנס ליה, כבוד מורנו הרב מוהר"ר „יעקב ישראל" נקרא „יעב"ץ" זצלה"ה, אב"ד דק"ק עמדן יע"א, בן לאותו צדיק הגאון הגדול החסיד המפורסם חכם הכולל אדמ"ו הרב מוהר"ר „צבי" נקרא „חכם צבי" זצללה"ה אב"ד דג"ק אה"ו יע"א; נשמתו יצאה בקדושה ביום וי"ו עש"ק א' דר"ח אייר תקל"ו לפ"ק וגופו נקבר בו ביום סמוך לכניסת ש"ק. נ'צ'ב'ה תחת כנפי השכינה כזוהר הרקיע מזהירה [א].
וכל הערים הקרובות והרחוקות, מקום אשר שמע מות הגאון יעב"ץ הגיע, היה בכי ואבל גדול ליהודים, כי אבד איש צדיק ואיש אמונים מן הארץ; והמדקדק הגדול ר' שלמה דובנא, יצא לקונן בשיר קינה, הנדפס מיד בעיר ברלין בשם אבל יחיד [ב], כי הגאון יעב"ץ ז"ל היה יחיד בדורו, ובכל נפשו יצא לקנא קנאת ה' צבאות, ושפתי חנף שנא, ואל אדם לא יכנה, לזכר עולם ינון שמו.
[א] וראשי החרוזים מן המצבה הם: "יעקב ישראל".
[ב] ור"ש דובנא עשה בס' אבל יחיד פרט על שנת מות הגאון יעב"ץ בהמלות, ואי"ך אתנח"ם, שעולה תקל"ו.

Mightiest of the shepherds and most eminent of the Sanhedrin: on the day he was taken the sun went down, and the pure candlestick was put out.
For him it is fitting to weep and to make lament, for he was a wall for us in the day of wrath and fury, "trouble as of her that brings forth her first
child" (Jer. 4:31).
He is the great and famous gaon, expert in all the chambers of the Torah, in the revealed and in the hidden and in all the sciences — "no secret was
too hard for him" (cf. Dan. 4:6) — the honoured our teacher the rabbi R. "Jacob Israel", called "Ya'avetz", the memory of the righteous and holy be for
a blessing for the life of the world to come, head of the court of the holy community of Emden, may God protect it; son of that righteous man, the
great gaon, the famous pious man, the all-embracing sage, our master and teacher the rabbi R. "Tzvi", called "Ḥakham Tzvi", the memory of the righteous
and holy be for a blessing, head of the court of the Three Communities A[ltona], H[amburg] and W[andsbek], may God protect them. His soul went out in
holiness on the sixth day, the eve of the holy Sabbath, the first day of the New Moon of Iyyar 5536 [1776] by the short count, and his body was buried
on the same day, near the coming in of the holy Sabbath. May his soul be bound in the bond of life, under the wings of the Shekhinah, shining "as the
brightness of the firmament" (Dan. 12:3) [a].

And in all the towns, near and far, wherever the news of the death of the gaon Ya'avetz arrived, there was weeping and great mourning for the Jews, for
a righteous man and a man of faith was lost from the earth. The great grammarian R. Solomon Dubno went out to lament in a dirge, printed at once in the
city of Berlin under the name Evel Yaḥid ("Mourning for an only one") [b]; for the gaon Ya'avetz, of blessed memory, was unique in his
generation, and with all his soul he went out to be zealous with the zeal of the Lord of hosts; he hated flattering lips, and gave flattering titles to no
man (cf. Job 32:21). "May his name be continued for ever" (Ps. 72:17).

An ornamental rule ends the text.
Kahana's notes

[a] The initials of the lines of the tombstone are: "Jacob Israel" (יעקב ישראל).

[b] And R. Solomon Dubno made in the book Evel Yaḥid a chronogram of the year of the death of the gaon Ya'avetz in the words ואי"ך אתנח"ם ("and how
shall I be comforted"), which come to [5]536 [1776].

P. 6, at the beginning of note a, read: "At the head of those who wrote to him from there with questions was the gaon R. Moses", etc.

P. 9, line 8: "the eminent pious man, our teacher R. Sh. A., of righteous memory" — he is the pious rabbi our teacher R. Samuel, author of the
responsa Devar Shmuel and of the book Ha-Zikhronot.

P. 20, line 10: "the rabbi R. W., head of the court of the province of Fiyehem(?)" — he is the rabbi R. Benjamin Wolf son of R. Aaron Simeon Spira.
See the text of his tombstone in the book Gal'ed (§ 65) and the note of R. Sh. Hak.

Ibid., line 11: "Afterwards he married the daughter of the gaon, head of the court of Prague" — he is the rabbi the gaon R. David Oppenheim; see
below, p. 82. In the year 5473 [1713], when his first wife died, he took Shifrah, daughter of the rabbi R. Benjamin Wolf, as his wife. See the book
Gal'ed (§ 80, p. 43) and the note of R. Sh. Hak.

P. 92, to note b one should add: "This R. Samson Wertheimer is the relative by marriage of R. B. K., mentioned above, p. 21."

P. 93, line 10: מפ"ר, abbreviation: "because of wickedness".

P. 102, line 2 from the bottom: לה"ב, that is: "to Hamburg".

P. 135, lines 2, 3: "that also in the holy community of P. the head of the court, our teacher R. Y. Katz" — he is R. Jacob Katz, mentioned before
(p. 76), and the holy community of P. is Frankfurt-on-Oder.

P. 146, line 16: "R. W. Halevi" — his name is R. Wolf Halevi, and he was parnas and leader of Altona.

P. 147, line 15: "Sh. b. R. A. Kh."; in the manuscript is written: "Sh. b. R. A. K." (perhaps one should correct: "Sh. b. R. A. N."), and he is the one
mentioned above, p. 50, who served Ḥakham Tzvi. He was the son-in-law of R. Zalman Norden, as explained on p. 80, and according to this he was the
brother-in-law of the brothers Norden, who are R. L. and Reuben, sons of R. Zalman Norden, who lived in London, as explained above, p. 94. (Note of R.
Tzvi Hirsch Jaffe.)

P. 152, line 5 from the bottom: "to the leader R. D. at the time they travelled to the fair of P. B." (his name was R. David, as explained in the gloss
on p. 161; and "L. D." is perhaps an abbreviation for "Lewarden". Note of R. Tzvi Hirsch Jaffe). P. B. is Pressburg.

P. 187, lines 10, 11 from the bottom: "On the 18th of the first Adar, my wife gave birth to a male child for me, on the eve of the holy Sabbath, and
I brought him into the covenant on the holy Sabbath, [portion] Mishpatim." (These words are not exact, for the Sabbaths in the first Adar of 5518
[1758] were these: the 3rd of the month, portion Terumah; the 10th, portion Tetzaveh; the 17th, portion Ki Tissa; and the 24th, portion
Va-Yakhel. Note of R. Tzvi Hirsch Jaffe.)

P. 200, line 20: "Mazu'a Julius" — he is the man Julius mentioned on p. 183.

P. 203, to note c one should add these words: "And besides these books, the gaon Ya'avetz did wonders in the work of vocalising the Mishnah and the
Talmud, and his works Luaḥ Eresh, Seder Tefillah and Leḥem Shamayim testify that he was one of the great grammarians."


צד 204 לשורה 10, יש להעיר שמכאן נראה איך הגאון יעב"ץ הגה יומם ולילה בתורת ה' . ופעם ישב להגות בספרי קדש באמצע הלילה, ותנומה נפלה על עפעפיו, ואור הנר עומד לפניו, ויפול פחם מהנר הדולק על הספרים והכתבים אשר עסק בהם, ותאכל האש סביביו, ובאשר ערבה לו שנתו לא הרגיש מאומה, ונשרפו כמה כתבים ודפים ונעשו אפר, וכמעט היתה השלהבת אוחזת בשערות ראשו, ויקץ יעקב משנתו ויחרד עד מאד, וכאשר שבה נפשו אליו, וידע את חסד ה' כי גבר עליו, אשר הציל אותו ואת כתביו, ואלו הן הנשרפים הם המה שהיו נדפסים מכבר, והיותרת אשר עדן לא יצא לאור עולם היה לאוד מוצל מאש. הנה נס בתוך נס! עיין בס' „מור וקציעה" (ח"א בסופו ד' ק"ג).
עמוד 211 שורה 23 הרב ר"א, בעמוד הקודם כתוב עליו „כמוה' יצחק", והאמת שנקרא שמו ר' איצק (=יצחק) הורוויץ, וכן הוא החרוז על מצבתו „איצק הלוי". עיין נוסח מצבתו בס' „אגדת פרחים" לוויטטקאווער (צד 287 סי' ט').

P. 204, line 10: one should remark that from here one sees how the gaon Ya'avetz meditated day and night in the Torah of the Lord. Once he sat
meditating on holy books in the middle of the night, and sleep fell upon his eyelids, with the candle standing before him; and a coal fell from the
burning candle onto the books and writings he was occupied with, and the fire ate around them; and since his sleep was sweet to him he noticed
nothing. Several writings and leaves were burnt and turned to ash, and the flame almost took hold of the hair of his head, when Jacob awoke from his
sleep and trembled exceedingly. When his soul returned to him, he knew the Lord's kindness upon him, who had saved him and his writings; and those
that were burnt were the very ones that had already been printed, and the remainder, which had not yet come out to the light of the world, was "a
brand plucked out of the fire". Behold a miracle within a miracle! See the book Mor u-Ketzi'ah (part 1, at the end, fol. 103).

P. 211, line 23: "the rabbi R. I." — on the preceding page is written of him "our teacher R. Yitzḥak", and the truth is that he was called R.
Itzik (= Yitzḥak) Horowitz; and so the acrostic on his tombstone is "Itzik ha-Levi". See the text of his tombstone in the book Iggeret Peraḥim by
Wittkower (p. 287, § 9).

An ornamental rule ends the list. The lower half of scan 252 is blank.
